      • substitute

        @Nullable
public static org.bukkit.Material substitute(@Nonnull
                                                       com.cryptomorin.xseries.XMaterial xMaterial)
        A sensible substitute Material that exists on the running server for an XMaterial that doesn't (e.g. NETHERITE_BLOCK -> DIAMOND_BLOCK on 1.8), or null if there is no mapping. Used as a smarter fallback than a generic placeholder for guide/category icons.

      • stack

        @Nonnull
public static org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack stack(@Nonnull
                                                            com.cryptomorin.xseries.XMaterial xMaterial)
        Builds an ItemStack from an XMaterial, substituting FALLBACK when the material does not exist on the running (legacy) server. Replaces the unsafe new ItemStack(xMaterial.parseMaterial()) idiom, which throws NullPointerException on legacy servers where XMaterial.parseMaterial() returns null.
        Parameters:
        xMaterial - The XMaterial to resolve
        Returns:
        A non-null ItemStack

      • isVanillaFurnace

        public static boolean isVanillaFurnace(@Nullable
                                       org.bukkit.Material material)
        Whether the given Material is a vanilla furnace, treating the legacy lit-furnace material as equivalent. On 1.8-1.12 an actively burning/smelting furnace is a separate material, BURNING_FURNACE (id 62), distinct from the unlit FURNACE (id 61); the 1.13 flattening merged them into FURNACE with a lit block state. Code that gated on type == Material.FURNACE therefore silently ignored any lit furnace on legacy servers (breaking the EnhancedFurnace speed/efficiency/fortune, which only act while it is burning). Blast furnaces and smokers are deliberately excluded (exact name match).
        Parameters:
        material - The Material (may be null)
        Returns:
        Whether it is a vanilla furnace (lit or unlit) across versions

      • isPlaceableBlock

        public static boolean isPlaceableBlock(@Nullable
                                       org.bukkit.Material material)
        Whether the given Material can be placed as a block, version-aware.

        On 1.13+ this is just Material.isBlock(). On legacy versions (pre-1.13) some placeable blocks only have an item form whose isBlock() returns false - most importantly SKULL_ITEM (player/mob heads), which Slimefun uses for the vast majority of its machine blocks. Those are treated as placeable here so head-textured machines can register and function on 1.8-1.12 instead of being rejected.

        Parameters:
        material - The Material (may be null)
        Returns:
        Whether it can be placed as a block
